paragraphs: Anomaly detectors often learn what normal data look like from a training set assumed to be clean. If that set already contains unnoticed anomalies, the learned distinction can become unreliable. EPHAD addresses this problem after training, by adjusting a detector’s outputs using evidence available when new examples arrive.

The framework combines information already captured by the trained detector with an additional source of evidence. That source can be a multimodal foundation model such as CLIP, a classical anomaly detection method, or knowledge specific to the application. This makes the contribution a way to revise existing predictions, rather than a requirement to rebuild the original training process.

The authors explain the approach with a synthetic example and evaluate it on eight visual datasets, twenty-six tabular datasets, and an industrial dataset. They also examine hyperparameters and different contamination levels. The reported results support robustness across the tested detectors and evidence combinations, suggesting that useful external evidence can help compensate for contaminated training data at deployment time.
neurips-2025-an-evidence-based-post-hoc-.tldr: EPHAD adjusts anomaly detector outputs at test time using additional evidence to counter the effects of contaminated training data.

paragraphs: Foundation models for physical systems face a structural problem: data from different partial differential equations can have different numbers of dimensions. An architecture built around one fixed dimensionality does not naturally transfer across all these systems. Setting a maximum dimension or maintaining separate encoders introduces inefficiencies that complicate sharing a model across physics tasks.

The paper introduces the Axial Neural Network, or XNN, to handle varying tensor dimensionalities within a shared architecture. Its design draws on parameter sharing ideas associated with Deep Sets and graph neural networks. The aim is to reuse learned computation across dimensional settings while retaining computational efficiency, making dimensionality less of an architectural constraint.

The authors convert existing PDE foundation models into XNNs and study training from scratch, pretraining across multiple PDEs, and fine-tuning on one PDE. Their experiments report competitive performance against the original models and better generalization to unseen dimensions. These findings support both the architecture and the value of exposing physics foundation models to multiple dimensionalities during pretraining.
neurips-2025-axial-neural-networks-for-d.tldr: Axial Neural Networks share computation across tensor dimensionalities, matching existing PDE models competitively while generalizing better to unseen dimensions.

paragraphs: In adaptive experiments, bandits, and reinforcement learning, earlier observations influence which data are collected next. This dependence complicates uncertainty estimates. Bayesian calculations remain appealing because their procedure looks much like the familiar independent-data case, but using that procedure does not by itself establish that its uncertainty statements have valid frequentist behavior.

The paper extends the Bernstein–von Mises theorem to adaptive data collection. It establishes that, asymptotically, Bayesian uncertainty quantification matches Wald-type frequentist uncertainty quantification as the prior’s influence disappears. Crucially, this equivalence does not require the standard stability condition used to establish validity for Wald-type methods.

That distinction produces both a positive and a negative result. Under stability, the equivalence supports frequentist validity of Bayesian uncertainty estimates. When stability fails, however, the paper shows that Bayesian uncertainty can remain asymptotically invalid even though the prior washes out and the two procedures agree. Simulations support both conclusions. The central lesson is that agreement between uncertainty methods and independence from the prior are different properties from statistical validity.
neurips-2025-bernsteinvon-mises-for-adap.tldr: For adaptive data, Bayesian uncertainty can asymptotically match Wald estimates without being frequentist-valid when stability fails.

paragraphs: KL divergence measures a difference between probability distributions and is used to compare language models during tasks such as fine-tuning and distillation. Computing it exactly for arbitrary language models is intractable, so practitioners estimate it from samples. A standard Monte Carlo estimate is unbiased, but individual estimates can fluctuate substantially and even become negative despite KL divergence itself being nonnegative.

The authors introduce a Rao–Blackwellized estimator that preserves unbiasedness while provably having variance no greater than the standard estimator. This separates two desirable properties: being correct on average and being stable across repeated estimates. They also derive an analogous estimator for the KL gradient, allowing the same approach to influence model training directly.

In sentiment-controlled fine-tuning experiments, the proposed method substantially reduces variance and yields more stable KL estimates. Its gradient estimator also stabilizes training. Models trained with it more frequently lie on the reward-versus-KL Pareto frontier, meaning they more often achieve tradeoffs that competing tested models do not improve on both dimensions simultaneously.
neurips-2025-better-estimation-of-the-ku.tldr: A Rao–Blackwellized KL estimator preserves unbiasedness, guarantees no greater variance, and improves training stability in sentiment-controlled fine-tuning.

paragraphs: Neural Radiance Fields usually learn a three-dimensional scene from camera observations, modeling how light traveling through the scene produces pixel colors. This paper asks whether a related representation can recover environmental structure from other signals. Radio and audio also carry information about their surroundings, even though their sensors do not produce ordinary images.

The main obstacle is multipath: a sensor receives a mixture of signals that have undergone different environmental reflections. Inferring the scene therefore requires interpreting that mixture. The authors redesign the NeRF approach so it can learn from multipath measurements, extending the scene-learning idea beyond the optical relationship between objects and camera pixels.

Their concrete application is recovering an indoor floorplan from sparse WiFi measurements collected at multiple locations in a home. The learned floorplans are described as promising, preserving the exploratory strength of the result. They also support forward uses, including predicting indoor signals and basic ray tracing. Together, these outcomes suggest that a learned scene representation can connect wireless measurements with useful information about indoor structure.
neurips-2025-can-nerfs-see-without-camer.tldr: A redesigned NeRF learns promising indoor floorplans from sparse WiFi multipath measurements and supports signal prediction and basic ray tracing.

paragraphs: Gaussian Splatting represents visual content using Gaussian primitives and supports efficient rendering of three-dimensional scenes. Its use has also expanded to images, videos, and dynamic scenes. Applying artistic styles to these representations remains challenging, particularly when the desired change involves more than recoloring the existing content.

CLIPGaussian provides one framework for text-guided and image-guided stylization across images, videos, three-dimensional objects, and dynamic four-dimensional scenes. It modifies the Gaussian primitives directly and can be inserted into existing Gaussian Splatting pipelines. The method does not require a large generative model or training the underlying representation again from scratch.

For three-dimensional and dynamic scenes, the approach jointly optimizes geometry and color, enabling style changes to affect structure as well as appearance. For video, it achieves temporal coherence while preserving model size. The authors report superior style fidelity and consistency across the evaluated tasks. The contribution is a shared stylization mechanism across several content types, with changes made in the representation already used for rendering.
neurips-2025-clipgaussian-universal-and-.tldr: CLIPGaussian directly edits Gaussian primitives to provide text- or image-guided style transfer across images, videos, 3D objects, and dynamic scenes.

paragraphs: Diffusion models trained on imbalanced datasets often generate less varied and lower-quality examples for rare classes. This paper investigates what happens inside the model when some classes dominate training. It focuses on latent representations at the bottleneck of the U-Net, where information used during generation is represented internally.

The authors identify substantial overlap between the latent subspaces of rare classes and those of common classes. They connect this overlap to feature borrowing, in which rare-class generation draws on features associated with dominant classes. Their analysis indicates that relative class imbalance contributes to the problem beyond the effect of having few examples of a particular class.

CORAL addresses this overlap through supervised contrastive losses that encourage class representations to separate. The intervention therefore targets the organization of the latent space during learning. Experiments report significant improvements in both diversity and visual quality for rare-class samples compared with state-of-the-art methods. The findings connect an internal representational problem to a training objective designed to reduce it.
neurips-2025-coral-disentangling-latent-.tldr: CORAL separates overlapping class representations in diffusion models to improve the diversity and quality of samples from underrepresented classes.

paragraphs: Dermatology image datasets can miss important differences in disease prevalence, skin tone, and everyday clinical settings. DermaCon-IN addresses this representation problem with images collected prospectively in outpatient clinics in South India. It contains 5,450 clinical images from 2,993 patients, grounding the resource in the conditions encountered in Indian outpatient care.

Board-certified dermatologists provide annotations spanning 245 diagnoses. These diagnoses are organized in a hierarchy based on disease causes, using a taxonomy adapted from Rook’s classification. This structure gives the dataset a clinically organized set of labels while capturing a broad range of conditions and skin tones present in the sampled setting.

The authors benchmark convolutional networks, vision transformers, and Concept Bottleneck Models. These evaluations establish starting points for later research and explore incorporating anatomical and concept-level information into predictions. The contribution is both a dataset and an initial experimental foundation for more interpretable, clinically realistic dermatology AI. Its relevance comes from representing outpatient cases and populations that existing resources may inadequately cover.
neurips-2025-dermacon-in-a-multiconcept-.tldr: DermaCon-IN provides dermatologist-annotated images from South Indian outpatient clinics and benchmarks models for more clinically representative dermatology AI.

paragraphs: Optimization methods can differ in how quickly their losses improve as model size and computational resources increase. This paper studies those scaling relationships for stochastic momentum algorithms in a power law random features model. The analysis varies data complexity, target complexity, and model size, revealing four distinct shapes of training loss curves.

Within this setting, conventional stochastic gradient descent with momentum has the same scaling exponents as stochastic gradient descent. The proposed dimension-adapted Nesterov acceleration, or DANA, changes momentum hyperparameters according to model size and data complexity. This adaptation improves the scaling exponents across a broad range of the studied data and target complexities, including compute-optimal scaling behavior.

The authors validate their theoretical predictions with experiments on high-dimensional synthetic quadratic problems. They also report improved loss exponents over SGD in large-scale text experiments using LSTMs. These results connect a theoretical scaling advantage with an observed advantage in a practical sequence-modeling setting. The central finding is that adapting momentum to problem structure can change scaling behavior, beyond the effect of conventional momentum.
neurips-2025-dimension-adapted-momentum-.tldr: DANA adapts momentum to model size and data complexity, improving scaling exponents theoretically and in synthetic and LSTM experiments.

paragraphs: Chain of thought increases inference-time computation through sequential token generation. This paper studies padding tokens as another way to supply computation without adding model parameters. Its results concern a specific formal architecture: transformers with averaging-hard attention and masked pre-normalization, supplied with a polynomial number of padding tokens.

For these transformers, the authors prove an exact correspondence with FO-uniform TC0, a class of extremely parallelizable problems. A known upper bound is matched by a new lower bound, establishing both what the architecture can express and its boundary. The proof uses padding to bring complete problems and reductions from classical complexity theory into transformer analysis.

The paper then adds looping, which dynamically increases depth at inference time. With O(log^d n) looping, the padded architecture recognizes exactly FO-uniform TC^d. Allowing polylogarithmic looping yields FO-uniform NC, a broader class associated with efficient parallel computation. These are expressiveness results for the specified formal model. They motivate investigating padding and looping as parallelizable forms of test-time computation alongside sequential reasoning.
neurips-2025-exact-expressive-power-of-t.tldr: The paper exactly characterizes how polynomial padding and inference-time looping expand the expressive power of a specified transformer architecture.

paragraphs: Eye movements during reading provide information that can be studied together with the text being read. EyeBench creates a benchmark for models that use these paired inputs to predict cognitive and linguistic properties. Its purpose is to make an underexplored intersection of machine learning and cognitive science easier to enter and evaluate systematically.

The benchmark brings multiple datasets and prediction tasks into a standardized evaluation framework. Tasks include assessing reading comprehension and detecting developmental dyslexia. This breadth lets researchers study different uses of reading-related eye tracking within a common evaluation setup, rather than treating every dataset and task as a separate implementation project.

EyeBench is released as an open-source package containing data download and harmonization scripts, baseline and state-of-the-art models, and evaluation code. These components provide the infrastructure for comparing predictive approaches. The authors identify adaptive interfaces, personalized education, and better understanding of language processing as directions that progress could support. The immediate contribution is the shared benchmark and software foundation for pursuing those goals.
neurips-2025-eyebench-predictive-modelin.tldr: EyeBench standardizes evaluation of models that combine reading eye movements and text to predict cognitive and linguistic information.

paragraphs: Transformers contain many attention heads, but their contributions to particular concepts are not always easy to identify. This paper investigates whether individual heads specialize in semantic or visual attributes. It studies both language-only and vision-language models that generate text, looking for interpretable structure within their attention layers.

The method builds on probing intermediate activations with the model’s final decoding layer. The authors reinterpret this practice using signal processing, which gives them a principled way to combine information across multiple samples. They then rank attention heads according to their relevance to target concepts, connecting internal measurements to specific attributes of interest.

The results show consistent head-level specialization across the studied model types. Editing as few as 1% of heads selected by the method can reliably suppress or enhance target concepts in the reported experiments. Evaluations cover question answering, toxicity mitigation, image classification, and captioning. The contribution therefore combines a tool for locating concept-relevant heads with evidence that these selected heads offer a useful point of intervention.
neurips-2025-head-pursuit-probing-attent.tldr: Head Pursuit ranks concept-relevant attention heads and shows that editing as few as 1% can control targeted concepts in tested models.

paragraphs: Associative learning links items that occur together, potentially changing how those items are represented internally. Studying such changes in biological systems is difficult. This paper adapts an associative learning paradigm from cognitive neuroscience to language models, using in-context learning to examine representational changes across six models.

The initial findings show a non-monotonic pattern consistent with the Non-Monotonic Plasticity Hypothesis: moderately similar items become more differentiated after learning. The authors then use the controllability of language models to investigate another influence, called vocabulary interference. This measures how the associated items overlap with the wider vocabulary and captures competition between new associations and prior knowledge.

Higher vocabulary interference amplifies differentiation in the experiments. The findings suggest that representational change depends on both the similarity between the items being learned and their competition with a broader representational environment. The proposed scientific role for language models is therefore as accessible systems for testing and generating hypotheses about memory reorganization. Consistency with a neuroscience hypothesis provides a connection to human learning without establishing identical underlying mechanisms.
neurips-2025-large-language-models-as-mo.tldr: Experiments across six language models connect associative representational changes to item similarity and interference from the broader vocabulary.

paragraphs: Image segmentation usually identifies objects from a predefined set of categories. Reasoning segmentation goes further by producing masks from complex language requests that may refer to objects implicitly. The authors find that existing models struggle with this task on remote-sensing imagery, motivating resources and a model specifically for geospatial analysis.

They introduce GRES, containing 27,615 annotations across 9,205 images, and PreGRES, a pretraining collection assembled from existing datasets with more than one million question-answer pairs across 119,279 images. Their benchmark model, LISAt, combines scene description, detailed question answering, and segmentation from natural-language prompts within a vision-language system.

The reported evaluations show gains over prior geospatial foundation models on visual description and over open-domain models on reasoning segmentation. Specifically, the abstract reports a 10.04% BLEU-4 improvement over RS-GPT4V and a 143.36% gIoU improvement over open-domain models. These findings establish an initial geospatial benchmark and show the value of addressing remote-sensing language-and-image tasks directly, with both dedicated data and a corresponding model.
neurips-2025-lisat-language-instructed-s.tldr: LISAt introduces geospatial training resources and a vision-language model that describes satellite scenes, answers questions, and segments objects from complex prompts.

paragraphs: Training a language model to be helpful, honest, and harmless involves objectives that can support or conflict with one another. One approach mixes training data for these goals. Another combines the parameters of models that have specialized separately. This paper systematically compares these two routes to balanced alignment.

The analysis examines previously overlooked cooperative and conflicting relationships among the three objectives. It considers how mixing data handles conflicts during training and how model merging handles them at the parameter level. The authors then propose Reweighting Enhanced task Singular Merging, or RESM, to address problems encountered when merging models aligned to these preferences.

RESM uses outlier weighting and sparsity-aware rank selection to tackle accumulated preference noise and adaptation to sparsity across layers. Extensive evaluations report gains of 2%–5% over previous data mixture methods and 1%–3% over previous merging methods. The findings support RESM’s effectiveness and robustness in the tested alignment settings, while positioning parameter merging as a practical approach to balancing multiple behavioral objectives.
neurips-2025-mix-data-or-merge-models-ba.tldr: RESM combines specialized models with noise- and sparsity-aware merging to improve the tested balance of helpfulness, honesty, and harmlessness.

paragraphs: Images captured in adverse weather can contain complex degradation that models trained on synthetic data with fixed parameters struggle to handle. This paper addresses both the starting training data and the ability to adapt restoration decisions. It introduces HFLS-Weather, a physics-driven dataset designed to simulate diverse weather phenomena with high fidelity.

The dataset initializes a reinforcement learning framework with two levels of control. Locally, weather-specific restoration models are refined through perturbation-driven image quality optimization. This supports reward-based learning without paired supervision. Globally, a meta-controller chooses which restoration models to use and determines their execution order based on the degradation in the scene.

These two levels address complementary decisions: how individual restoration models improve and how their use is coordinated for a particular image. The authors report continuous adaptation to real-world conditions and state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of adverse weather scenarios. The contribution is a combined training and control strategy that connects a high-quality synthetic starting point with adaptive restoration at both model and workflow levels.
neurips-2025-real-world-adverse-weather-.tldr: A physics-driven weather dataset initializes reinforcement learning that refines restoration models and adapts their selection and execution order.

paragraphs: The paper studies how to recover an underlying distribution and denoise observations in multivariate Gaussian mixture models. It allows both shared noise levels and observation-specific noise covariances. This matters because observations can differ in how uncertain they are and in which directions that uncertainty is concentrated.

Instead of following the conventional maximum likelihood approach, the authors treat each observation as a temporal slice of a family of stochastic diffusion processes. They introduce a score-based objective that explicitly models the latent distribution and incorporates each observation’s noise covariance. Reverse-time dynamics then provide a principled route to denoising through multiple steps.

The theoretical result gives a near-parametric score estimation error rate of polylog(n)/n for n independent observations, improving on existing diffusion results. Empirically, the method outperforms nonparametric maximum likelihood estimation for both density estimation and denoising fidelity, particularly in high dimensions. Together, these findings support diffusion modeling as a promising way to perform nonparametric empirical Bayes estimation while accommodating unequal noise across observations.
neurips-2025-score-based-diffusion-model.tldr: A generalized diffusion framework learns latent distributions and denoises Gaussian observations with unequal noise, with theoretical error guarantees and empirical gains.

paragraphs: Pretrained foundation models have helped robotics, but their use for low-level control often centers on imitating demonstrations. This paper proposes two stages of post-training that let robots move from supervised learning into autonomous practice. The first stage combines behavioral cloning with predicting how many steps remain until task completion.

Those steps-to-go predictions serve a second purpose during self-improvement: they support a shaped reward function and a success detector. A fleet of robots can then practice downstream tasks with minimal human supervision. This connects supervised task understanding to the feedback needed for further learning through interaction.

Experiments with real and simulated robots report greater sample efficiency and higher success rates than increasing imitation data collection for supervised learning. Ablations identify the combination of web-scale pretraining and self-improvement as central to the efficiency gains. The authors also demonstrate autonomous acquisition of novel skills that generalize beyond behaviors in the imitation datasets. The results support a route from pretrained capabilities and demonstrations toward broader skill learning through practice.
neurips-2025-self-improving-embodied-fou.tldr: Steps-to-go prediction turns supervised robot training into a foundation for autonomous practice, improving efficiency, success rates, and novel skill acquisition.

paragraphs: In episodic reinforcement learning, regret measures the performance lost while learning which actions to take. This paper analyzes the Monotonic Value Propagation algorithm for tabular Markov decision processes. Its bound depends on action suboptimality gaps, which describe how far an action’s value falls below the optimal value at a particular state and step.

The analysis also accounts for conditional total variance: the randomness encountered along trajectories conditioned on visiting a particular state at a particular step. This gives a more localized characterization of learning difficulty than overall trajectory randomness. A new analysis of weighted suboptimality gaps produces a regret bound that combines these gaps with the conditional variance measure and planning horizon.

A complementary lower bound shows that dependence on conditional total variance is necessary, even when maximum unconditional total variance approaches zero. Thus, low overall randomness does not eliminate the difficulty associated with learning particular state-and-step pairs. The authors suggest their analysis could potentially extend to other algorithms. The established result concerns MVP and clarifies which form of environmental randomness must appear in these regret guarantees.
neurips-2025-sharp-gap-dependent-varianc.tldr: New regret bounds for MVP show why action gaps and variance conditioned on specific state visits both matter for learning difficulty.

paragraphs: Strong results in mathematics, physics, and computer science do not fully describe a language model’s academic knowledge. SuperGPQA broadens evaluation to graduate-level knowledge and reasoning across 285 disciplines. It addresses gaps in coverage of specialized fields, including light industry, agriculture, and service-oriented subjects that existing benchmarks inadequately assess.

The benchmark uses an iterative filtering process combining language model responses with expert feedback. Its purpose is to remove questions that are trivial or ambiguous while refining the evaluation material. The project also involves more than eighty expert annotators and an interactive human–LLM system, making large-scale annotation management part of the methodological contribution.

In the reported evaluation, Gemini-2.5-Pro achieves the highest accuracy at 63.56%, leaving substantial room for improvement across the benchmark’s diverse domains. The result shows that strong performance in familiar academic areas can coexist with broader knowledge and reasoning gaps. Alongside the questions themselves, the authors provide insights from coordinating annotation at this scale to help guide similarly broad evaluation projects.
neurips-2025-supergpqa-scaling-llm-evalu.tldr: SuperGPQA evaluates graduate-level knowledge across 285 disciplines, revealing substantial gaps beyond the academic areas emphasized by existing benchmarks.

paragraphs: Language models retain keys and values from earlier tokens so they can use that information during generation. As sequences grow, this key-value cache consumes substantial memory. Tensor Product Attention, or TPA, addresses the storage burden by representing queries, keys, and values through compact tensor decompositions.

The mechanism factorizes these representations into contextual low-rank components and integrates with Rotary Position Embedding. The paper uses TPA to build the T6 transformer architecture. Its goal is to make attention representations more economical while retaining or improving model quality, linking the representation used inside attention to the resources needed during inference.

Language modeling evaluations show that T6 matches or surpasses tested transformers using multi-head, multi-query, grouped-query, and multi-head latent attention. Comparisons cover perplexity and established evaluation benchmarks. The authors also report memory and decoding computation efficiencies that enable longer sequences under fixed resource constraints. The contribution therefore combines a compact attention mechanism with empirical evidence that reducing inference overhead can coexist with competitive language modeling performance.
neurips-2025-tensor-product-attention-is.tldr: Tensor Product Attention compresses attention representations and the KV cache while matching or improving tested transformer performance.

paragraphs: Some neural networks operate on structured geometric spaces rather than ordinary Euclidean vectors. Attention has been extended to such spaces, but many existing designs are specific to one geometry. This paper seeks a shared mathematical framework that can support attention across several kinds of matrix manifolds.

The proposed Gyro Attention framework uses gyrovector structures, which extend vector addition and scalar product to manifolds. Several important matrix geometries admit these structures, including symmetric positive definite, symmetric positive semi-definite, and Grassmannian manifolds. By expressing attention through the shared gyrovector structure, the method can apply across these geometries without defining its overall framework around only one of them.

The authors instantiate GyroAtt using three gyro structures on the positive definite manifold, three on the positive semi-definite manifold, and one on the Grassmannian manifold. Experiments on four EEG datasets demonstrate the framework’s effectiveness. The contribution is both a general formulation and a set of concrete realizations showing how one attention approach can operate across multiple matrix geometries.
neurips-2025-towards-a-general-attention.tldr: GyroAtt uses shared gyrovector structure to formulate attention across multiple matrix manifolds, with effectiveness demonstrated on four EEG datasets.

paragraphs: Some AI videoconferencing systems transmit compact representations of a speaker’s pose and expression, then synthesize video at the receiving end. This saves bandwidth but permits puppeteering attacks, where an adversary controls another person’s apparent identity in real time. Ordinary deepfake detection is poorly suited to this setting because legitimate video is also synthetic.

The proposed defense examines the transmitted latent representation for biometric information that remains alongside pose and expression. A metric-learning approach disentangles those identity cues from the intended motion information. The resulting identity evidence enables detection of unauthorized swaps using features already shared during the system’s normal operation.

Experiments across multiple talking-head models show consistent improvements over prior defenses. The authors also report real-time operation on consumer GPUs and good generalization to out-of-distribution data. These findings support the practicality of checking latent identity information within the tested systems. The key insight is that identity leakage in a representation intended to convey motion can become useful evidence for identifying impersonation.
neurips-2025-unmasking-puppeteers-levera.tldr: A biometric defense detects videoconferencing impersonation by extracting identity cues that leak into transmitted pose-and-expression representations.

paragraphs: LLM judges are commonly validated by comparing their ratings with a single reference label aggregated from human ratings. The paper identifies a problem with this procedure: some evaluation criteria reasonably permit more than one rating for the same item. It calls this rating indeterminacy, which forced-choice instructions conceal by requiring everyone to select only one answer.

Humans and language models may resolve that ambiguity differently even when their judgments are reasonable. The authors develop a framework connecting agreement metrics, ways of eliciting ratings, and aggregation schemes. Their approach uses multi-label response sets to record multiple acceptable ratings, allowing validation to account for ambiguity instead of collapsing it immediately into one label.

Experiments span eleven real-world rating tasks and nine commercial language models. Standard forced-choice validation selects judges that perform as much as 31% worse than those selected with the response-set approach. The finding shows that the rating collection procedure can materially affect which judge appears best. It supports treating acceptable alternatives as part of validation evidence.
neurips-2025-validating-llm-as-a-judge-s.tldr: Allowing multiple reasonable ratings improves LLM judge selection by accounting for ambiguity that forced-choice validation can distort.

paragraphs: Generating a coherent three-dimensional scene requires objects to make sense individually and remain consistently arranged across viewpoints. Existing approaches face difficulties with spatial reasoning, viewpoint control, or consistency between views. VIPScene explores using knowledge of the physical world encoded in video generation models to improve scene synthesis.

The framework accepts text or image prompts and combines video generation, feedforward three-dimensional reconstruction, and open-vocabulary perception. These components support semantic and geometric analysis of objects in the scene. The approach uses video as a source of information for constructing layouts and placements that remain coherent when viewed from different positions.

The authors also introduce First-Person View Score, an evaluation measure that uses a continuous first-person perspective and the reasoning ability of multimodal language models to assess coherence and plausibility. Experiments report significant improvements over existing methods and good generalization across diverse scenarios. The paper thus contributes both a scene-generation framework and an evaluation approach oriented toward how a scene holds together as the viewpoint moves.
neurips-2025-video-perception-models-for.tldr: VIPScene combines video generation, 3D reconstruction, and perception to synthesize coherent scenes from text or images.
